reasoning.text: Reproducibility is solid on the numeric core (q, N, psi/omega/Ninv, Barrett constants, negacyclic flavor are all pinned and both impls agree), but the spec leaves the paper's signature structures — the conflict-free bank/offset map, crossbar permutation, twiddle-ROM addressing, and an internally contradictory radix-4 mult count and FSM — to guesswork, so the impls converge functionally yet reconstruct rather than transcribe those pieces. The biggest fidelity gap is that the two defining CFNTT contributions are not faithfully reproduced: the conflict-free mapping is an invented XOR-fold and the 33%/20% optimized radix-4 schedule is replaced by a naive 3-mult butterfly, leaving a correct generic negacyclic NTT rather than the specific accelerator.
gaps: [operation] The paper's actual conflict-free bank-index and offset functions (Sec. III headline result is not transcribed; both impls reconstructed an XOR-fold)
[control] Per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s routing table
[operation] Twiddle-ROM address function f(stage,block) under the rearranged twiddle-reuse loop
[operation] Whether the optimized radix-4 butterfly uses 2 or 3 modular multiplications (datapath fields say 3, op-count reconciliation says 2)
[param] Naive-radix-4 add/sub baseline (assumed 10) that anchors the 20% reduction claim
[control] Exact FSM transition table, radix-2 vs radix-4 sequencing, and wiring of the DONE state (two contradictory fsm lists given)
[operation] Exact Barrett post-reduction bound / number of conditional subtractions (<2q vs <3q, <=2 subs)
[control] Internal coefficient ordering (natural vs bit-reversed) between NTT output and INTT input
